prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues to direct E3 ubiquitin ligases to proteins of choice.

statement.case_for: I opened with B005 because condensates are a physical-chemistry idea I know well, but my colleagues' evidence moves me. Six of eight members placed targeted protein degradation in their top three, and the case holds up on chemistry. A small molecule becomes a bridge that uses the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery, so occupancy-based pharmacology gives way to event-driven, catalytic removal of a target. The molecular-glue arm also gives a mechanistic explanation for thalidomide-type drugs through cereblon. The concept is original, many laboratories have confirmed it across many targets, and it has opened a large field. A single prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa spans the conceptual PROTAC invention and the mechanistic cereblon discovery.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved yet, so the committee could be accused of rewarding a modality on the strength of trial results. The three-person cap also forces an uncomfortable cut. Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto and Ito all made contributions that are hard to rank below the chosen three. The PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages are arguably two achievements joined under one citation, and the allocation between them is not settled.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B057 second but names Ciulli rather than Handa as third laureate, because Ciulli gave the VHL chemistry and ternary-complex mechanism. He notes that molecular-glue credit is a separate matter.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli argument seriously. The ternary-complex work is the chemistry that makes PROTAC design rational, and as a physical chemist I value it. I still lean to Handa, because a prize that explains thalidomide's mechanism ties the two arms together under one citation. With Ciulli in place of Handa, the glue arm falls out and the citation would have to narrow to PROTACs. I would like to hear whether the committee prefers a PROTAC-only citation or one that covers both arms. I do not think the Handa-versus-Ciulli choice is settled.

responses.point: Aili ranks B057 first and B005 second. He values the bridge between molecular design and biology, and sees condensates as tying sequence and multivalency to cell function.
responses.response: I agree on both. Our overlap on peptide and protein self-assembly is why I put B005 first. Honest consideration of maturity makes me hesitate. The field still argues over how much cellular function needs true phase separation, and over in vitro versus in vivo interpretations. Credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is also contested. B057 is better resolved on both counts, and the clinical data are arriving. I keep B005 as my first alternative, not as a competing preference, and I would not block B057 for it.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B068 (Buchwald and Hartwig, Pd-catalysed C-N coupling) first. He argues that it is mature, general and widely used, and that the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover C-N coupling.
responses.response: The practical reach is not in doubt, and the timing argument is fair. My reservation is conceptual novelty. The 2010 prize already recognised palladium cross-coupling as a method class, and the earlier tin-amide work of Kosugi and Migita complicates the priority question. That does not make B068 unworthy, but it ranks below B057 for me, where the molecular concept is new. I would want to see how Somfai handles Kosugi in a final configuration.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks the Car-Parrinello method (B037) first, describing it as an original and overdue foundation of ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and reactions.
responses.response: The scientific quality is high and the two-person attribution is clean, which I admire. I did not rank it, and I will say so plainly. I cannot judge it by the standard I would apply to my own field. Only one member put it first, so it is hard to see it winning a majority. If Aqvist can show how it connects to current chemistry, such as condensed-phase and biomolecular simulation, I would listen. For now it is not my preference.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the absence of an approved degrader drug as too early for a prize.
Whether the third laureate should be Handa (molecular glue and cereblon) or Ciulli (VHL and ternary-complex chemistry), and whether the citation should span both arms.
Whether two distinct achievements (PROTACs and molecular glues) would be better recognised as two separate prize parts.
How B005 credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag could be resolved if the committee returned to condensates.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict is apparent from my profile. I am at Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but that is a shared institution, not a personal tie to any candidate. My research on lipid self-assembly, lipid-protein co-assembly in amyloid and membranes overlaps scientifically with B005 and B064, which I ranked first and second. I disclose this because it could colour my judgement of those ballots. B057 has no such connection.
